To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have observed a threshold in the core of the tokamak for long wavelength electron temperature fluctuations and that this threshold is consistent with the theoretical prediction for the threshold of ∇T(e) -driven trapped electron modes.

the threshold for the onset of electron temperature fluctuations in a tokamak is determined by the electron temperature gradient, that the threshold is independent of toroidal rotation, that electron heat transport is stiff above the threshold, and that the threshold can be explained by the trapped electron mode.
we have observed a critical threshold for the first time for a turbulent quantity in the DIII- D tokamak core and have shown that the threshold is consistent with trapped electron mode turbulence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how turbulence in the core plasma of tokamaks limits the confinement of heat and particles and thus the performance of fusion plasmas.
the development of new techniques for the measurement of the turbulent fluctuations of electron temperature in tokamak plasmas.
the development of a new type of magnetic field sensor, based on the Faraday effect in a magnetic fluid.

the critical gradient for trapped electron mode turbulence is a local property of the plasma, and is not set by a global stability threshold.
